newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy not ready "to see soldiers die" in Albania.
newsitem.headline: Italy not ready "to see soldiers die" in Albania.

text.p: Italian Defence Minister Beniamino Andreatta said on Saturday foreign military intervention in Albania would require the support of rebels as well as the government, adding he was not prepared to "see Italian soldiers die".

In a speech to parliament, he said Western military action would bring inevitable casualties and that Italian military planners had estimated that the size of any force would have to be similar to that in Bosnia.

"I am not ready to see Italian soldiers die to prove the point that there is a legitimate government in Albania," Andreatta told a joint meeting of the lower house defence and foreign affairs commissions.
He said a request made by Albania's new unity government, formed this week to try to halt armed anarchy rocking the Balkan state, was not sufficient grounds for sending a force.
"We are asking the Albanian government, as a premise for international intervention, to bring on board the people who have authority over the populations of the cities and villages," he said.
Several Western countries, including Germany, have made clear they are sceptical about the international community sending a force to restore order in Albania.
Ambassadors of Europe's top security body agreed in Vienna on Saturday to give broad support to sending foreign troops.

The 54-nation Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) backed a proposal by OSCE mediator Franz Vranitzky to ask foreign governments to send forces, but no individual state gave an explicit commitment to do so.
